intro.author: Obadiah, whose name means 'servant of the LORD'; nothing else is known about him
intro.written: Most scholars date it soon after Jerusalem's fall in 586 BC; some place it earlier, after a previous attack on Jerusalem
intro.audience: The people of Judah, though the oracle is addressed to Edom
intro.setting: Edom, the nation descended from Jacob's brother Esau, lived in the rugged mountains south-east of the Dead Sea. When Babylon sacked Jerusalem, Edom gloated, looted the city and handed over refugees, a betrayal Judah never forgot.
intro.purpose: To announce that God would judge Edom's pride and cruelty against its brother nation, and that his kingdom would prevail.
intro.bigIdea: 'As thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee,' and 'the kingdom shall be the LORD's.'

outline.title: Edom's pride will be brought down
